documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group, visit 01/12/2021 (in person).
Type 1 diabetes, doing well back in the classroom with hybrid teaching. A1c 7.0%. Rare mild lows. Injection sites rotated, no lipohypertrophy.
Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro per correction scale, ibuprofen as needed. NKDA.
BP 114/72. Monofilament normal both feet. Urine microalbumin normal.
Plan: continue. Return 6 months.

documents.title: COVID vaccine question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Does type 1 diabetes put me in an earlier group for the COVID shot? I'm also back in the classroom so I'm not sure which group I fall under. Thanks!

documents.title: RE: COVID vaccine question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. Both count. Type 1 diabetes is on the state's list of conditions, and teachers have their own phase too, whichever opens first for you. The state sign-up site and the larger pharmacies are booking; we don't have supply in the office yet. Please send us the dates once you have them so we can add them to your chart.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group, office visit 07/06/2021.
Type 1 diabetes, age 27. Summer break, more activity, two mild lows a week now that she is hiking. A1c 6.9%. Reviewed treatment of lows with fast carbohydrate.
Meds: insulin glargine 24 units nightly, insulin lispro by correction scale, ibuprofen PRN. NKDA.
Exam: BP 112/70, weight stable, feet intact.
Plan: reduce lispro the meal before long hikes, basal unchanged. Follow up in 6 months.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal influenza vaccine IM L deltoid. No adverse reaction observed. Reminded her the annual is overdue, front desk to call.

documents.body: Hi Lauren, please upload it here. Your physical was in February 2020, so the doctor can sign it from that, but she'd really like to see you for a check-up this spring. I filled in your immunizations including the COVID doses. Form will be ready for pick-up or sent back here by Friday.

Outside endocrinology group. Seen 02/01/2022.
She is well. A1c 7.2% (01/25). Download reviewed, overnight readings flat on glargine 24 units, post-lunch spikes on school days.
Current medications: glargine, lispro, ibuprofen as needed. No known allergies.
BP 110/68. Feet normal. Eye exam reported up to date without retinopathy. Urine microalbumin and lipids normal this year.
Plan: pre-bolus lunch 15 min earlier. Next visit summer.

orders.reason: chronic loose stools, bloating, weight loss, vesicular rash

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, she is at home after school; identity and consent confirmed.

CC: loose stools for a few months.

Since about July: 3-4 loose stools a day, lots of bloating and gas, worse later in the day. Clothes looser, she thinks she's lost about 5 pounds without trying. Tired, though she blames back-to-school. Also an itchy rash on both elbows and the fronts of the knees, little blisters that she scratches open. No blood in stool, no fever, no vomiting. No travel, no antibiotics. Glucose readings more erratic, some lows after meals she didn't absorb.

On video: rash on elbows shown to camera, clusters of small excoriated papules and a few vesicles, symmetric. Appears thin but comfortable.

FH matters here: maternal aunt with celiac, she has T1DM.

A/P: chronic diarrhea with weight loss and a symmetric vesicular extensor rash in a T1DM pt with a family history of celiac. Celiac high on the list; the rash fits dermatitis herpetiformis. Referring to GI for serology and endoscopy rather than piecemeal testing here. Asked her NOT to start a gluten-free diet before GI sees her, it makes testing unreliable. Told her to let endo know about the post-meal lows. Will come in for flu shot next week.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Influenza L arm, bivalent COVID booster R arm. Both tolerated. GI referral status checked for her: appointment 11/11 with outside GI.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY ASSOCIATES
New consult, seen 11/11/2022. Referred by her primary care physician for diarrhea and rash.

HPI: 28-year-old teacher with type 1 diabetes. Several months of loose stools, abdominal bloating and weight she did not intend to lose. She has noticed the bloating is clearly worse after bread or pasta. Persistent tiredness. Itchy, blistering rash over both elbows and knees.

PMH: type 1 diabetes (endocrinology). Heavy menstrual periods.
Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime; insulin lispro with meals by scale; ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for cramps.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: father with type 1 diabetes; mother with autoimmune thyroiditis; maternal aunt with celiac disease.
Social: never smoker, alcohol rarely, preschool teacher.

Exam: Weight 50 kg. Thin young woman, pale. Abdomen soft. Skin: clusters of tense small vesicles over the extensor elbows and knees, some excoriated.

Labs today: Hgb 9.8 g/dL, MCV 74 fL. Iron 30 mcg/dL, TIBC 450 mcg/dL, ferritin 15 ng/mL. Tissue transglutaminase IgA sent, pending.

Impression:
1. Chronic diarrhea, bloating, weight loss with gluten-related symptoms, strong family and personal autoimmune history: celiac disease suspected; serology pending.
2. Rash typical of dermatitis herpetiformis.
3. Microcytic anemia with low iron indices.

Plan: We will call with the tTG. If positive, upper endoscopy with duodenal biopsies. Please continue a normal gluten-containing diet until biopsies are taken. The anemia needs evaluation and iron replacement; we would appreciate your team managing this. Letter copied to patient.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: Gastroenterology Result Letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology, result communication.
Tissue transglutaminase IgA 142 U/mL (reference under 15), strongly positive. Discussed with Ms. Cote by phone 11/17: findings are consistent with celiac disease. Upper endoscopy with duodenal biopsies recommended to confirm before lifelong diet change. She would prefer to schedule it during a school break; she understands she should keep eating gluten until then. Our schedulers will contact her.

documents.title: GI visit and your blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Lauren, I got the GI notes. Sorry about the celiac news, though it explains a lot, and it is very treatable. They also found your blood count is low and your iron stores are low, which likely accounts for some of the tiredness. I'd like to see you in the office to go over the anemia and start treatment. The front desk will reach out; early January is fine if December is hard with school.

documents.title: RE: GI visit and your blood count
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. December is crazy with the holiday program, I'll take the first week of January after school. I'm still eating normally like GI said.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group, seen 12/06/2022.
Type 1 diabetes with newly found celiac disease by serology (GI note reviewed). More post-meal lows and unexplained highs this fall, likely from variable absorption. A1c 7.4%. Lispro timing changed to right after meals while GI symptoms are active. Glargine unchanged at 24 units. Celiac makes us watchful for thyroid disease as well; thyroid testing was normal this year. NKDA.
Return in 3 to 4 months.

documents.title: Diabetic Eye Examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Optometry, exam 12/13/2022. Dilated fundus exam: no diabetic retinopathy or macular edema either eye. Glasses prescription unchanged. Return 12 months.
